name: family Hager
forbes_bio: Philipp Hager is a major shareholder of Hager SE.
The company is a leading provider of solutions and services for electrical installations, covering business fields such as energy distribution, cable management, and building automation.
Hager SE generates consolidated group revenues exceeding $3.5 billion annually.
Originally founded as a GmbH, the company has a history spanning over three decades and transitioned into a Societas Europaea (SE) in May 2007.
The group operates internationally with a workforce exceeding 13,000 employees and manages well-known brands such as Hager, Berker, and E3/DC.

name: Nutchamai Thanombooncharoen
forbes_bio: Nutchamai Thanombooncharoen is cofounder and chairman of SET-listed Carabao Group, maker of energy drink Carabao Dang.
Nutchamai branched out from her family's financial services business to team up with Sathien Sathientham for a property venture before jointly setting up Carabao.
In 2002, they partnered with popular folk singer Aed Carabao for a foray into energy drinks.
Top international markets for Carabao include Cambodia, China, Myanmar, Vietnam and Afghanistan.
In 2023, she got into beer brewing through Tawandang Brewery in partnership with Sathien.
forbes_facts: She also has a stake in Tawandang Distillery, which makes rice whisky.
In 2020, Carabao launched a new vitamin C-infused drink called Woody C+ Lock in orange and lemon flavors.

name: John Edson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2005-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
forbes_bio: Over the course of selling two boat-building companies, John Edson (d. 2019) built a fortune of more than $1 billion.
An entrepreneur who loved the water, Edson first dipped his toe in business by selling used boats.
He purchased the brand name "Bayliner" for $100 in 1955 and started a company to build affordable plywood motorboats.
The business grew into a yacht-manufacturing powerhouse, and Edson flipped the firm to The Brunswick Corporation in 1986 for $425 million.
Six years later, Edson bought another yacht maker, Westport Yards, which he sold in 2014 for an undisclosed amount.
forbes_facts: John Edson worked a paper route and earned enough to build his first boat at age 13.
After selling Bayliner, Edson took a few years to cruise the world aboard his 161-foot boat Evviva (Italian for "long live").

name: Jeffrey Soffer
forbes_bio: Jeffrey Soffer is one of seven children of Donald Soffer, who developed the Florida city of Aventura.
Alongside his sister Jackie, Soffer helmed the family real estate firm, Turnberry Associates, for over two decades.
In 2019, Soffer set out on his own, bringing his interests under new company Fontainebleau Development.
Soffer's real estate holdings include the historic Fontainebleau Miami Beach luxury hotel.

name: Li Liufa
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2015-2024); Hurun Global (2016-2025); Hurun China (2008-2024)
forbes_bio: Li Liufa chairs the Tianrui Group of China, whose business includes steel, tourism, cement and minerals.
Li worked at a fertilizer factory in Henan Province in the late 1970s before setting up his first business -- a small steel casting factory.
Li holds an EMBA degree from Peking University.

name: Dani Reiss
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2019-2021); Hurun Global (2020)
forbes_bio: Dani Reiss took over as CEO of outerwear company Canada Goose in 2001.
His grandfather, a Polish immigrant, launched the Toronto-based retailer as Metro Sportswear in 1957.
Today the company is known for its down jackets, which cost over $1,000 and are a favorite among celebrities like Bradley Cooper and Emma Stone.
Reiss took Canada Goose public in March 2017; he owns about 18% of the stock.
He has pledged to keep manufacturing in Canada and employs more than 3,400 people.
forbes_facts: His first business venture, in high school, was buying baseball cards he thought were undervalued and trying to sell them at a profit.
In the early 2000s, Reiss walked down Queen Street in Toronto trying to get stores to carry his coats. Every single one said no.

name: Paulo Setubal Neto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2019); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Paulo Setubal Neto is a member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
He is the oldest son of Olavo Setubal, an industrialist, banker and politician, who was mayor of São Paulo, Brazil's largest city.
He inherited a nearly 2% stake in Itausa, the parent of Itau-Unibanco, Latin America's biggest private sector bank.
He owns more shares at Itausa, the bank's holding company, than any of his 7 siblings; he served on the Itausa board for decades.
His brother Roberto Egydio Setubal was president of Itau Unibanco from 1995 to 2017.

name: Jean-Paul Clozel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2022); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Jean-Paul Clozel and his wife Martine Clozel cofounded Swiss biotech firm Actelion in 1997 with three other colleagues.
The husband-and-wife team sold the company to Johnson & Johnson for $30 billion in 2017.

Actelion makes drugs for orphan diseases, which affect fewer than 200,000 people
and typically receive little research funding.
Following the Johnson & Johnson acquisition, the couple spun out publicly-traded Idorsia, which they now run together.
Idorsia is specializing in the discovery and development of small molecules to eventually develop drugs to treat insomnia, lupus and other diseases.
forbes_facts: To start Actelion, the Clozels reportedly sold their house and worked out of a rented garage in the company's early days.
Jean-Paul is a trained cardiologist and Martine is a trained pediatrician.

name: Xu Guozhong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Xu Guozhong chairs Jiangsu Guomao Reducer, a Chinese motor manufacturer.
Xu founded the processor of Guomao in Jiangsu Province in 1993.
Son Xu Bin, 32, is Guomao's general manager.
